The abundance data give the silicon‐to‑hydrogen ratio in each star relative to the Sun.

**Star 1**  
\[
[{\rm Si/Fe}]_1 = +0.3\;{\rm dex},\qquad [{\rm Fe/H}]_1 = 0\;{\rm dex}
\]
\[
[{\rm Si/H}]_1 = [{\rm Si/Fe}]_1 + [{\rm Fe/H}]_1 = +0.3\;{\rm dex}
\]

**Star 2**  
\[
[{\rm Mg/Si}]_2 = +0.3\;{\rm dex}\;\Rightarrow\;[{\rm Si/Mg}]_2 = -0.3\;{\rm dex}
\]
\[
[{\rm Mg/H}]_2 = 0\;{\rm dex}
\]
\[
[{\rm Si/H}]_2 = [{\rm Si/Mg}]_2 + [{\rm Mg/H}]_2 = -0.3\;{\rm dex}
\]

The logarithm of the ratio of silicon abundances between the two stars is the difference of their \([{\rm Si/H}]\) values:

\[
\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{(n_{\rm Si}/n_{\rm H})_1}{(n_{\rm Si}/n_{\rm H})_2}\right) = [{\rm Si/H}]_1 - [{\rm Si/H}]_2 = (+0.3) - (-0.3) = 0.6
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{n_{\rm Si,\,1}}{n_{\rm Si,\,2}} = 10^{0.6} \approx 3.98 \;\approx\; 3.9 .
\]

(The stellar masses are not needed for this abundance ratio.)

**Answer: D**.
